approachAdjustment: Mostly sound. verdictReason: Nothing equivalent exists (no Canvas tab, no Space-scoped authoring path), and the item already places ownership in Data Plane as the adoption plan does; only the principal stamping and the missing Control decision need correcting.

verdictReason: The user-facing feature is absent, but a cheaper per-turn path already exists in the main composer and the Space import pipeline is built for connectors; the item should be rephased around that and corrected on the Control personal-Space limit and the ACL grant requirement.

Only per-feature typed error states exist (for example SpaceRoomComposer onError, :458-467, and the code-keyed copy in shared/i18n/errors.ts).

constraints: Frontend Plane only, but a forced reload must not drop an unsent composer draft, so it depends on the draft store. Telemetry must not carry message content or user data and must respect ZDR (ids only). The browser reaches the gateway only through nginx /api/ and /health (nginx.conf proxy locations), so a gateway /version at the root is not reachable by the SPA without a new /api route.
approachAdjustment: Fix one pointer: apps/gateway/src/domains/monitoring.rs is Quarry change-monitoring (URL check, latest, history), not an observability sink, and observability.rs only exposes server Prometheus metrics. There is no client error or boot-stage endpoint and no global request-id in the envelope, so add a small ids-only client-diagnostics route under /api/v1 (or drop the boot-stage recorder from this item) and add request-id middleware if the failure card must show one. Everything else in the approach (root and region boundaries with Errored, one-time reload on chunk-preload failure with a sessionStorage guard, version.json with no-store plus an explicit nginx location and index.html no-cache, gateway min-client header or client-config, non-blocking banner, forced reload only on contract mismatch) is sound.
effortNote: Raised from S. Boundaries plus chunk recovery plus a build-id banner is S; the gateway contract-version header, a client-diagnostics route and draft-safe forced reload make the full item M.
verdictReason: Nothing of this exists in production code, so the recommendation stands, but it points at the wrong gateway route for observability and understates effort.

verdictReason: The item accurately states today's gap (always-on model turn, single mention, no human post, no policy writer) and nothing equivalent exists; only the implementation placement needs the corrections above.

constraints: The mention signal must be content-free and ZDR-safe, and the recipient must pass the room read entitlement. The gateway cannot produce it: notification-core allows the verevon-gateway principal only to notify the delegated user and only as notification.created (handlers.go:150-170,199-218), so a notification for a different member must come from an owner-plane producer (Model Plane session-core event or Application Plane projection) consumed by notification-core, not from a widened gateway allowlist. Binding an agent from a mention is owner/manager-only (CREATE_AGENT_ROLES), so a regular member can only request an invite; a mention never grants authority. Agents are org-scoped definitions today (agents table has orgId, optional createdBy), so "an agent you own" is only an approximation.
approachAdjustment: Replace 'add a content-free space.mention type to the Space sender's allowlist' with: persist mention records in the user entry metadata at append time, emit a Space/session event from the owner plane, and add a notification-core consumer in the style of conversation_followed_message.go that creates the in-app notification per mentioned member after a read-entitlement check. Keep the gateway path to validation of mentioned_person_refs against the Control roster. Make invite-from-mention a role-aware flow: owner/manager can bind and send, others get a request. Do not label the picker section 'your agents' until a personal-agent ownership notion exists beyond createdBy.
effortNote: Unchanged for people and agent mentions with mention records and a notification consumer; becomes L if @room/@here and role-gated user groups are in the same slice.
verdictReason: The gap is real and nothing equivalent exists, but the proposed notification mechanism contradicts how notification-core authorizes producers, so the approach must be rewritten around an owner-plane event consumer.

constraints: Model proposes browser actions and Quarry executes or rejects them under a Browser Broker grant; grants are broker-signed and the request cannot widen the domain policy (browser_run.rs:128-200). A Space run needs a Control decision bound to the room audience hash and revision before any grant is issued, and sessions must be forced to ephemeral or run-scoped profiles so a member's signed-in profile is never shared into a room. Browser runs are owner-bound (Quarry owner projection) and approvals belong to the run starter, so takeover must be restricted to the requester or an owner. Room agents are born tool-less and confirmation-only, so the binding policy must explicitly allow a browser tool. Run-level require_approval is unsupported (continuation unavailable), so approvals must use the per-action HITL path. ZDR: no frame retention, no persistent profile.

Do not rely on run-level require_approval. Keep sign-in profiles owner-only.
effortNote: Unchanged. Space plumbing and cards are M, the live preview with takeover, hand-off events and audience-authorized streaming bring it to L; teach-by-demonstration is a separate XL.
verdictReason: The room-scoped browser is absent, but the item's baseline wrongly says there is no hand-off or bot-wall classification and omits the existing takeover, HITL and challenge-signal building blocks that cut the real scope.

exactGap: A governed agent-to-owner action pipeline is built end to end for exactly one action, tickets.create: Control model-action-view and run-action-decision plus owner-effect reservation (run_action_decision.go:340-347, model_action_view.go:18-26), Capability Core advertising (capability-core model_action_view.go:21-32), the execution-core adapter (ticket_tools.rs) and approval continuation, all hard-coded to that one action and schema hash. MODEL_EXECUTABLE_ACTION_IDS has 8 entries and none of the 14 spaces.* registry actions (model-eligibility.ts:126-135, action-registry.ts:1991-2134); the Space actions catalogue is human-only (spaces.rs:4880-4925). Room agents are also born tool-less and confirmation-only, which strips tools and agentic mode on mention turns (spaceAgents.ts:540-565, spaces.rs:4519-4535).
reuse: Control RunActionDecision (run id, thread, Space ref, subject, schema hash, payload digest, idempotency key, audience revision, expiry) and OwnerEffectReservationCommitment: the existing per-call, run-bound authority, to be generalized instead of inventing a new grant type
tickets.create pipeline (ticket_tools.rs, capability-core model_action_view.go, execution-core approval continuation and approval_delivery_worker) as the template for each admitted action
Owner-issued agent-action-grants routes per conversation (spaces.rs:665-675) as the human-granted standing allowance
SpaceApprovalPanel and orchestration approvals as the in-room approval card
Model-Plane-owned operations (thread presentation lives in model-gateway/session-core) as same-plane tools that need no cross-plane grant
constraints: Model proposes, owner executes: each admitted action needs an owner-side endpoint that verifies a Control run-action decision and rechecks its own ACL (the run's thread authorization is explicitly not authority for a target resource, run_action_decision.go:19-22). Capability Core deliberately uses a server-owned schema, not a Frontend registry copy (capability-core model_action_view.go:29-32), so the Model Plane must not consume the Frontend action registry. Membership, role, deletion and credential-grant changes stay human-only (plan S3.6: agents may request use, never change future authority). Room agents are tool-less and confirmation-only by default and a run belongs to the member who started it, so approvals are decided by the run owner. ZDR forbids durable owner actions (personal_thread_decision.go:292-294).
approachAdjustment: Do not mint a new 'run-bound capability grant'; extend the existing run-action decision: add one runActionTarget entry per action (today only tickets.create is approved), generalize model-action-view and Capability Core from one fixed action to a server-owned list, and add an owner endpoint per owning plane. Do not have the Model Plane consume the Frontend registry: the registry feeds the browser (agent-tools.ts), while the Model Plane holds its own pinned schemas. Phase it: first Model-Plane-owned tools bound to the run's own thread (rename or pin the thread, post a card), which need no cross-plane decision; then Application-owned ones (pause self) and orchestrator-owned ones (schedule follow-up) through the run-action path. Also make binding policy editable, otherwise no room agent can use tools at all.
effortNote: Raised from M. Each action needs an owner endpoint, a Control decision target, a pinned schema and an execution-core adapter, and the single-action machinery must first be generalized.
verdictReason: The capability is genuinely missing for Spaces, but a run-bound decision mechanism already exists for one action and the item's grant and registry-consumption design conflicts with it; rewrite as generalizing that pipeline in phases.
